2.6.2 Hardware Verification Following Safety Complaint Level 1 (Type 1 CF)/As Reported Safety 2
  • Updated "When to Perform" section.

    • From: "FSEs are to perform hardware verification after a Type 1 CF is filed. Hardware verification may be waived if the customer admits to poor sample quality or operator error as the root cause of the erroneous result. Verification may also be waived if the customer is willing to run hardware verification including a system check and precision run. If applicable, document in the Oracle service request why service was waived. If service is not waived, then field service must perform system hardware verification as soon as possible."

      To: "FSEs are to perform hardware verification after a Safety Complaint Level 1 (Type 1 CF) is filed. Hardware verification may be waived if the customer admits to poor sample quality or operator error as the root cause of the erroneous result. Verification may also be waived if the customer is willing to run hardware verification including a system check and precision run. If applicable, document in the ServiceMax work order or Oracle service request why service was waived. If service is not waived, then field service must perform system hardware verification as soon as possible."

  • Updated "Background" section.

    • From: "When a Type 1 CF is filed, the call center can generate a field service request, and field service must assess and verify the system hardware using this procedure. As part of the CF investigation, field service makes a reasonable effort to identify root cause during instrument inspection, repair, and verification. Field service documents the root cause of a Type 1 CF at the lowest level component reasonable to claim, preferably at the individual part number level, or if not impossible at the individual part then at the module level (for example, aspirate probes, spinner grippers, peri-pump tubing, fluidics). If multiple parts are replaced proactively, do not document them as the root cause unless there is clear evidence of malfunction. If the root cause is determined to be operator error, then document that in the service request (for example, operator did not seat aspirate probe correctly). If no cause is found, or the problem could not be reproduced, have the documentation reflect this conclusion.

      In some scenarios, the CF event cause might be apparent and easily resolved over the phone, but the customer refuses to perform the necessary verification steps and requests service. CRTS is an acronym used by Call Center meaning the customer refuses to trouble shoot over the phone. In these instances, field service is requested to go on site, or attempt again to troubleshoot with the customer over the phone. Any troubleshooting tasks and resolutions via phone contacts must be documented in Oracle. If there is a delay in the FSE ETA, the customer may be more willing to assume some of the actions."

      To: " When a Safety Complaint Level 1 (Type 1 CF) is filed, the call center can generate a field service request categorized as "As Reported Safety" (ARS) in ServiceMax or "Type 1 CF" in Oracle, and field service must assess and verify the system hardware using this procedure. As part of the CF investigation, field service makes a reasonable effort to identify root cause during instrument inspection, repair, and verification. Field service documents the root cause of a Safety Complaint Level 1 (Type 1 CF) is filed at the lowest level component reasonable to claim, preferably at the individual part number level, or if not impossible at the individual part then at the module level (for example, aspirate probes, spinner grippers, peri-pump tubing, fluidics). If multiple parts are replaced proactively, do not document them as the root cause unless there is clear evidence of malfunction. If the root cause is determined to be operator error, then document that in the service request (for example, operator did not seat aspirate probe correctly). If no cause is found, or the problem could not be reproduced, have the documentation reflect this conclusion.

      In some scenarios, the CF event cause might be apparent and easily resolved over the phone, but the customer refuses to perform the necessary verification steps and requests service. CRTS is an acronym used by Call Center meaning the customer refuses to trouble shoot over the phone. In these instances, field service is requested to go on site, or attempt again to troubleshoot with the customer over the phone. Any troubleshooting tasks and resolutions via phone contacts must be documented in ServiceMax or Oracle. If there is a delay in the FSE ETA, the customer may be more willing to assume some of the actions."

  • Updated "Completing the Verification" section step 2.

    • From: " Attach all the data files to the service request in Oracle or the CF, or e-mail the documentation to cfcomplaints@beckman.com. Documentation to include:"

      To: "Attach all the data files to the service request in ServiceMax, Oracle or the CF, or e-mail the documentation to cfcomplaints@beckman.com. Documentation to include:"

  • Updated the title of document from "Hardware Verification Following Type 1 CF" to "Hardware Verification Following Safety Complaint Level 1 (Type 1 CF)/As Reported Safety".

    • Edited the liquid waste drawer kit note at the beginning of the procedure:

      From: "The Liquid Waste Drawer Kit does not contain the door cover, slide rails, ground strap screw with star washer, and the chain screws. Save the rails, the door cover, the screws, and star washer from the existed drawer to install on the new drawer."

    • Existing step 2 became step 4.
      • Existing substep 2a has been revised and has become note in step 4 before step 4a.

        From: " a. Inspect the drawer kit.

        i. Check all components are attached. See Figure 1. for more details.

        ii. Check all tubing connections are correctly connected to the Selector Valves.

        iii. Check all valve connectors and weight sensor connectors are correctly connected to the Bulk Fluid Tray Interface PCB.

        iv. Removed the Bulk Fluid Tray Interface PCB cover to access the PCB and leave cover to the side. See the image below for references."

        To: "Note:
        • Inspect the drawer kit and confirm all components are present.
        • Confirm all tubing is correctly connected to the Selector Valves.
        • Remove the Bulk Fluid Tray Interface PCB cover to access the PCB.

        From: "Remove the Liquid Waste containers from the drawer and put them to the side."

        To: "Remove the Liquid Waste containers from the drawer and set them to the side."

      • Substep 2c has been revised and has become substep 4c:

        From: "Install the slide rails from the existed drawer to the new drawer."

        To: "Attach the inner slide rails to each side of the liquid waste drawer using 3 screws from the kit for each rail."

      • The rail notes in existing step 2c have been combined on substep 4c.
      • Substep 2d has been revised and has become substep 4d:

        From: "Install the door cover from the existed drawer to the new drawer."

        To: "Install the drawer cover to the drawer using 4 screws from the kit or reuse the screws from the removal of the existing cover from the instrument."

      • Revised substep 2e and it has become substep 4e:

        From: "Slightly insert the new drawer half way in."

        To: "Install the drawer by aligning the inner rails into the outer rails and push the drawer in."

      • Step 2f has become step 4f.
      • Revised step 2g and it has become substep 4g:

        From: "Install the Bulk Fluid Tray Interface PCB cover back on."

        To: "Re-install the Bulk Fluid Tray Interface PCB cover."

        From: "Route the Liquid Waste output tubing through the chain and connect to the Selector Valves input connector and remove the clamp."

        To: "Verify the Liquid Waste output tubing is routed through the chain and connect the tubing to the Selector Valves input connector. Remove any clamps on the tubing (if applicable)."

        From: "Screw in the Chain to the drawer."

        To:"Attach the chain to the drawer using screws (2) from the kit or re-use the screws that previously attached the chain to the drawer."

        From: "Note: Ensure the star-washer is installed with the screw."

        To: "Attach the ground cable to the drawer using the star washer and screw. Cable is attached to the inner side of the drawer where paint has been stripped from the hole."

14.3.2 Troubleshooting LAS Event/Error/Failure 3 Added "DxI Duplicate Tests Run for Samples on DxA Automation" troubleshooting section to the end of the document.

The troubleshooting section has been added to prevent any test from being repeated unexpectedly in the event of Remisol (Automation System Software) getting an out of sequence message from the DxI instrument. This is done by disabling the "DTS Aspiration Finished" feature and enabling "DTS Aspiration Started" feature in case metrics are tracked or both features can be disabled in case metrics tracking is not needed. These features are already available in the dashboard of the Automation line

  • Added step 4i to disconnect the main pneumatic tubing on the wash arm pneumatic valve assembly. This needs to happen before loosening the two 7/64-inch hex screws holding the luminometer to the analytical module housing which is in the following step.
  • Updated step 4d by adding wash collar or manifold as they are interchangeable based on the known information.
  • Added step 4e to disconnect the two pneumatic tubing on the air cylinder because they should be removed before removing the dispense probe plate and eject plate. The existing step 4e has become step 4f which is when the dispense probe plate and eject plate get removed.
  • Step 4e has become step 4f and added information related to three 3/16-inch hex screws based on the known information in step 8 on pages 9A and 9B in the SOP 84-907088 Rev AC.

    From:

    Remove the dispense probe plate and eject plate (one 5/32-inch button-head hex screw, two 3/16-hex screws).

    To:

    Remove the dispense probe plate and eject plate.

    Note:

    New dispense/eject plate has three 3/16-inch hex screws.

    Old dispense/eject plate has one 5/32-inch button-head hex screw, two 3/16- inch hex screws.
